reason: Throughout this passage, elite figures are portrayed unfavorably, particularly Pharaoh and the Egyptian court. Pharaoh is depicted as an oppressor who repeatedly refuses to release the Israelites despite God's plagues, his heart is hardened, and he stubbornly pursues the fleeing Israelites, ultimately leading to his army's destruction in the sea. His servants and the Egyptian magicians (חרטומי מצרים) are shown as complicit in oppression and as inferior to God's power, failing to replicate the miracles. The narrative consistently characterizes these elite as obstacles to God's will and as deserving of divine punishment. This negative portrayal of the ruling class and their allies is central to the Exodus narrative.
